title: Current MCP clients and the 1.5.1 fixes

intent.statement: Agents on current MCP clients (Codex and Claude Code, MCP 2025-06-18 through 2026-07-28) reach one correctly registered Disk Steward server with its evidence skill, get typed, correctable answers, and the defects found in the first real cleanup and the accepted rung-4 findings are fixed, released as 1.5.1.

success_evidence.description: The bundled MCP helper serves clients of MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless, server/discover), 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 over stdio, and its answers validate against the upstream schemas for the version each request uses.
Every tool declares an outputSchema that each of its answers conforms to, and invalid arguments come back as tool errors a model can correct.
Codex and Claude Code each get the Disk Steward evidence skill and exactly one server registration from the supported installer, with backup and rollback.

The defects found in use are fixed: the path filter no longer redacts ordinary names, explain_growth honours its limit, the retired scanner's convergence test is deterministic, and verification no longer reports Xcode's ibtoold daemon as a failure.
Disk Steward 1.5.1 is built from the verified input, notarized, installed and published with gate evidence.

constraints: Never delete, move or modify any user file; the helper stays read-only.
Never open the user's live stores from tests; verification runs in isolated snapshots.
Keep every existing tool name and the 2025-06-18 handshake working.
non_goals: MCP tasks, sampling, elicitation, roots or subscriptions.
A remote (HTTP) MCP server or a public plugin directory listing.

assumptions.statement: The 2026-07-28 wire format and the upstream schemas published for it are stable enough to implement and validate against.
The convergence flake is the probe folding a change receipt stamped after the sample's start into that sample.

nodes.title: Audit 1.5.1: current clients, fixes and release
nodes.summary: Verify the final candidate in isolation and packaged, then install the notarized 1.5.1 and exercise it through both eras and both installers before publishing.

acceptance_criteria.description: On the final candidate: the full isolated suite passes, every mutation red fails its target test, and the packaged helper answers server/discover, a 2026-07-28 tools/list and tools/call, and 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 sessions, with answers validating against the vendored upstream schemas and each tool's outputSchema.

The notarized 1.5.1 is installed on the maintainer's Mac: list_review_items accepts get_health's scope name, a cargo target reads as build output after a review, and the Claude and Codex installers leave exactly one registration and the skill for each client. Open material findings prevent pass.

nodes.title: Fix the defects found in use
nodes.summary: Stop the path filter redacting ordinary names, honour explain_growth's limit for changed directories, and make the retired scanner's convergence deterministic by ordering the sample's clock after its inbox drain.

acceptance_criteria.description: '.disk-steward-gate-659' survives the path filter in the MCP backend and the bundle exporter, while sk-/gh*_/AKIA tokens at a name boundary or after '=' are still redacted.
explain_growth returns at most its requested limit of changed directories (200 when absent) and says when it truncated.
A deterministic test reproduces the convergence race (a change receipt stamped after the sample's start) and passes after the fix; the store's publication-time invariant is unchanged.

required_evidence.description: Focused tests and mutation reds for each fix.

blockers: No impact records cover the audited change scope

nodes.title: Treat Xcode's ibtoold daemon as expected in verification
nodes.summary: After a build or archive launcher exits 0, stop surviving descendants whose executable is Xcode's own ibtoold under the selected developer directory, verify cleanup, and pass the stage with a note; any other survivor still fails it.

acceptance_criteria.description: A stage whose only survivors are the selected Xcode's ibtoold passes with the stopped daemon named; an unknown survivor, a failed launcher or unverified cleanup still fails. Lineage, identity rechecks and cleanup verification are unchanged.

required_evidence.description: Supervisor unit tests for both branches, reds, and a full candidate verification whose package stage passes.

nodes.title: Serve MCP 2026-07-28 alongside earlier versions
nodes.summary: Answer server/discover and stateless 2026-07-28 requests (per-request _meta version, resultType, ttlMs and cacheScope, -32022 for unsupported versions) while initialize-based sessions keep working, validated against vendored upstream schemas.

acceptance_criteria.description: A 2026-07-28 client discovers the server and lists and calls tools and reads resources without initialize; every response validates against the vendored upstream 2026-07-28 schema.

A 2025-11-25 or 2025-06-18 client negotiates through initialize as before, and its responses validate against the matching upstream schema; an unsupported 2026 version gets -32022 with the supported list.

required_evidence.description: Protocol tests per era against vendored upstream schemas, and reds.

blockers: No impact records cover the audited change scope

evidence.claim: MCP 2025-11-25 recommends input-validation failures as isError results; MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless (server/discover, per-request _meta version, resultType, ttlMs/cacheScope); Claude Code probes stdio servers with server/discover and Codex shows the model only structuredContent.

The installed 1.5.0 helper answered server/discover with -32002, invalid arguments with -32602, listed no tool titles and reported a fixed version; MCP polish f670058 fixed the first, third and fourth.

The descendant xcodebuild leaves after a successful CI build is /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/ibtoold --sending-client-environment, reparented to launchd; the supervisor stops it with cleanup verified and records launcher-exited-with-descendants.
evidence.source: Process diff around a CI xcodebuild on 2026-10-05 (scratchpad xcode-leftover.py); docs/reliability/evidence/MCP-POLISH-1.5.1/full/candidate.json

evidence.claim: The first real cleanup found three review-tool defects, fixed by HOTFIX-1.5.1 (c22f173), and the Codex installer writes both a config.toml block and a plugin that declares the same server.

decisions.question: Support MCP 2026-07-28 only, or alongside earlier versions?
decisions.choice: Serve both eras on one stdio helper: 2026-07-28 requests are recognised by the per-request protocol version in _meta; initialize-based sessions keep 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and older.
alternatives: 2026-07-28 only; rejected because Codex still initializes with 2025-06-18 by default.
Stay on 2025-06-18; rejected because the user asked for full support and Claude Code is rolling out server/discover probes.
decisions.rationale: Both target clients keep working whatever they negotiate.

decisions.question: How do both clients get the evidence skill?
decisions.choice: One SKILL.md source in Integrations; the Codex plugin bundles it and the Claude installer copies it into <config-root>/skills with the same backup manifest.
alternatives: Separate skills per client; rejected because they would drift.
decisions.rationale: One source of truth for agent guidance.

Decision: Track whole-volume capacity everywhere accessible, but persist detailed evidence only for configured roots, registered agent process trees, and bounded investigation windows — The hybrid model preserves unexplained-growth detection and agent attribution without creating an unbounded privacy and resource burden

Decision: Bundle one read-only Swift MCP stdio executable that delegates to the app-owned evidence service over a protected local IPC boundary — One connector minimizes duplication and attack surface while keeping database ownership, sanitization, and retention inside the application

Decision: Implement it as an advanced capability with explicit confidence semantics and retain a useful FSEvents/snapshot fallback — Entitlement approval is external and cannot be guaranteed; the product must remain honest and useful in its absence
Decision: No; it will explain, export, and recommend while all MCP tools remain read-only — Evidence trust and attribution accuracy must be established before introducing destructive operations

turning_points: Decision: Deliver a canonical launchable Xcode app and redesigned dashboard as the first increment, then add the direct-distribution pipeline as a cumulative second increment — The first increment is independently useful and reviewable in Xcode, while Apple credential availability remains an external release dependency

Decision: Use direct distribution outside the Mac App Store under Team G3P6TU385Y with the proposed com.marudankiji.disksteward product identity — It matches the user's requested distributable desktop utility and Apple's Developer ID and notarization path; permanent identifiers also remove current configuration inconsistency

Decision: Keep the standard app complete without Endpoint Security and retain the optional extension as a separately gated target until Apple grants the restricted entitlement — This preserves the product's proven fallback while avoiding a distribution blocker and retaining the future exact-provenance path

Decision: Lead with current free-space health and a concise growth assessment, then show monitoring state and recency, with evidence export as the single clear action — This aligns the small popover with the user's immediate decision while detailed evidence remains available through export and MCP

Decision: Use one persistent Agent Access state, default off on fresh installs, that starts or stops the private local IPC service; show the state with a native toggle while keeping monitoring and manual evidence export independent — A privacy control must enforce service availability rather than merely change presentation, and it should not mutate external client configuration or interrupt the app's core evidence collection

Decision: Use a visible rolling lifecycle: 7 days of raw detail, 30 days of hourly path and capacity summaries, 365 days of daily summaries, finite anomaly detail, deterministic oldest-first pressure compaction, and a 512 MiB default hard ceiling; preserve manual exports as user-owned files and expose lifecycle status through UI and a read-only MCP tool — The tiers preserve recent forensic detail and long-term growth trends, while explicit coverage and pressure records prevent an agent from mistaking compacted history for complete history

Decision: Persist immutable observation runs and state observations, reconcile them through stable file objects and time-bounded path bindings, atomically maintain a current-file projection, and attach provenance, session context, rollups, retention, exports, and coverage gaps as separate linked records — An event chain supplies history, the materialized projection answers current state, stable identity handles rename and path reuse, and explicit observation coverage prevents unavailable roots or capped scans from fabricating deletions

Decision: Repair the existing native-app increment with one shared evidence-usefulness contract, then run two bounded branches: durable scan-generation convergence and authoritative human-triggered export; require the current-candidate gate to inspect an actual menu-created bundle from a populated database — The current database proves detailed state exists but the user path omits it, while repeated entry-cap scans cannot yet establish change history. Both defects invalidate the first actor-visible increment and can be repaired independently without changing the final intent or weakening privacy, retention, or distribution controls

turning_points: Decision: Current baseline: the local correctness candidate builds; 238 isolated tests pass, including native CLI onboarding and bundled-helper checks. Original 213-test evidence and reproduced failures remain historical. Existing fixes must be re-established under brownfield inspections rather than assumed complete; no scale, soak, or release readiness is inferred. Cumulative ladder: Safe testing alongside a running application → Trustworthy current evidence across changes and lifecycle → Useful bounded monitoring progress → Responsive bounded local agent service → Useful and private evidence API → Safe reversible agent onboarding → Regression-assured repair candidate. Each later gate repeats earlier observable safety scenarios on the current candidate — Reject the alternatives because they miss reproduced correctness/configuration failures or hide amplification. First rung has actor-visible value: a running application remains queryable while another launch/test executes. Evidence fixes, resource redesign and client configuration changes retain separate rollback and audit boundaries. Early independent fixes can start after test isolation; gate order preserves cumulative proof

Decision: Order acceptance separately from implementation: replace only blanket OUTCOME510 start dependencies with integration-requires, and retain verified CONTRACT510 as a hard prerequisite. Preserve every gate, cumulative outcome dependency and material finding. Scoped fixture work may proceed ahead of foundation audit; no task can pass its audit before OUTCOME510 — All alternatives weaken assurance or expand product scope. Current isolation/ownership implementation is exercised by64 scoped fixture tests. The revision preserves all7requirements and7gates; source inspection also adds the exact backend/SQLite paths required to fulfill existing TASK541 effective-cancellation acceptance. Existing specific consumed-artifact dependencies remain hard and will be reevaluated only if evidence shows another cycle

Decision: Add one bounded ordered-delivery/lifecycle repair under OUTCOME520 and require its evidence at GATE529. Preserve every existing requirement, implementation node, cumulative gate and completed result. Do not hide the failure with a test sleep increase or infer resolution from a later green suite — An observed regression plus concrete task-per-event ordering/resource hazard belongs to existing trustworthy evidence and bounded work requirements. Endpoint bridge ownership and callback epochs form one independently testable boundary distinct from subprocess ownership and scanner lifecycle; no new system entitlement or feature is added. Test isolation remains enforced by CONTRACT510; acceptance still depends on OUTCOME510

Decision: Strengthen the existing TASK522 and TASK552 integration acceptance and required handoff, and GATE559 public interval proof. Extend TASK552 only to the exact provenance/export models and tests required to fulfill existing accurate-evidence intent. Preserve all nodes, seven requirements, seven cumulative gates and completed work; no new product capability or weaker gate — The two independent code paths are observed, not speculative. Existing lifecycle and public DTO tasks are the earliest actor-visible integration boundaries. Keeping their explicit evidence contracts avoids false completion and competing source ownership; updated impact/inspection records must cover the added attribution/export paths before audit. Scale, rollback, overnight and all prior gate obligations remain

Decision: Extend TASK522 to its exact delivery adapter and strengthen the existing suspended-callback proof. Serialize the last cancellation check and callback-based native submission on the same main actor as lifecycle transitions. Preserve all nodes, gates, original intent, file-hint acceptance and historical proof — The current adapter ignores cancellation after suspended permission work. Main-actor serialization supplies a precise before/after submission boundary without blocking the main thread during asynchronous system callbacks; fake-center tests avoid real notification permission changes. No core/schema scope added; future receipt design remains separately required within TASK522

Decision: Extend existing TASK522 to the exact collector/store/SQLite boundary and one package-owned publication fence. First reproduce receipt-during-preparation in a disposable store and serialize only the final commit with receipt acceptance. Then integrate bounded coalescing, per-root durable invalidation and restart/failure ownership through the concrete app path. Keep AC02 end-to-end proof mandatory — These alternatives do not establish the existing invariant or violate bounded-work safety. A final commit permit is an internal synchronization boundary, not a new filesystem snapshot promise; avoid SQLite busy retries under its lock and retain rollback checks. No schema/public API expansion, new framework dependency, or ownership overlap with another active task. All intent requirements and cumulative gates are retained; no whole-task completion from the core subpatch

Decision: Change TASK-531/TASK-532's requires edges to RESEARCH-530 and OUTCOME-520 into integration-requires: the storage tasks may start against the recorded research decision and design candidate, but cannot pass audit until RESEARCH-530 and OUTCOME-520 are verified. No gate, acceptance criterion or finding is weakened — See choice

Decision: Change TASK-572's requires edge to OUTCOME-560 into integration-requires, exactly as R11 did for the storage tasks: TASK-572 may start its rehearsal tooling and measurements against the current candidate, but cannot pass audit until OUTCOME-560 is verified, and its overnight soak evidence must be re-established on the final candidate at GATE-579. No gate, acceptance criterion, finding or control is weakened; the final-candidate requirement stays in AC-TASK-572-01 and INSPECT-GATE-579-* — See choice

Decision: No. AC-GATE-579-01 and EVREQ-GATE-579-01 now require the scale matrix, the migration/rollback rehearsal and at least one hour of real-time soak evidence on the candidate's product sources; the overnight requirement is removed and TASK-572's summary says 'a real-time soak of at least one hour'. FIND-OVERNIGHT is resolved by the existing scale matrix and the completed real-time soak rather than accepted. No node, edge, rung, gate ownership, finding severity or control is otherwise changed — See choice; direction recorded in EV-R13-OPEN-SOURCE-RELEASE-SCOPE

turning_points: Decision: Represent a build-output directory, a shared cache and a repository as one evidence object with aggregate size and no per-file rows inside it — Artifacts are reproducible and are cleaned as a unit, so per-file provenance inside them has no user value while costing three quarters of the rows. See EV-601-CORPUS

Decision: Project evidence: repository ignore and tracking rules where a repository exists, manifest-anchored output locations where it does not, outermost match only, and never a tracked directory — Git is decisive where present and caught real false positives; 56 percent of candidates have no repository, so a manifest fallback is required. See EV-602-GIT-ORACLE

Decision: No. They form the final rung, after objects are trustworthy and visible, and they stay opt-in — Ordering keeps each rung demonstrable and keeps scope widening an explicit user choice. See EV-603-SHARED-CACHES

Decision: Refuse explicitly with the shortfall and the available remedies, and review the default limit against the object model's measured cost — The installed app demonstrates the failure: fourteen times the scope processed with no publication and repeated forced eviction. See EV-604-STUCK-SCAN

Decision: A new rung-1 task, TASK-615, owns wiring the probe and converging an installed store. It is validation-required by GATE-619, so rung 1 cannot pass without it — See EV-R1-UNWIRED-PROBE: the capability exists in the core but nothing in the product calls it

Decision: Keep the three cumulative increments and all six verified task contracts. TASK-616 establishes safe descendant supervision before any further candidate execution. TASK-617 repairs live dashboard/alert consistency in the first increment. GATE-619 accepts neither increment-1 safety nor its visible behavior until both repairs pass; later gates inherit both scenarios — User approved the two-task repair replan. The final object-model intent, success evidence and non-goals remain unchanged; no signing, installation or release is authorized

Decision: Baseline: installed 1.2.1 still samples capacity but has an incomplete detail scan and a reported frozen dashboard. Source at b7e3675 has six verified object-model tasks; no increment gate has passed. Rung 1: a safely supervised runnable candidate completes a representative scan or honestly refuses an over-budget scope, and its capacity/growth/last-alert display updates coherently. Rung 2: add measured, fresh and explained reclaimable objects in app/MCP. Rung 3: add shared caches only after opt-in. Each rung retains its own existing gate and repeats earlier proofs on the same candidate — OUTCOME-610 -> OUTCOME-620 -> OUTCOME-630 -> INTENT-006 remains the cumulative hierarchy. Dependencies order acceptance; independently scoped object sizing can proceed after supervision is verified, without claiming rung 1 has passed

Decision: Replace the always-on per-file scanner with three independent engines: a capacity ring that never touches the detail store; a directory-level FSEvents change journal with persisted sinceWhen that yields capped dirty sets; and an on-demand bounded review that prunes at classified objects and persists objects and reports, never files. Every table has a write-time cap and every reader a window, bounding the store at 32 MiB — Measured unit cost times corpus size exceeds any reasonable cap, while a metadata walk with object pruning answers the user's question in about 30 s without persisting files

Decision: Baseline: installed 1.2.3 (8) from the hotfix branch samples capacity, but its scan cannot converge, MCP summary tools are refused and capacity history is evicted; main at 345c072 adds verified object classification and pruning (TASK-611/612) and verification containment and dashboard consistency (TASK-616/617), with no rung passed. Rung 1 (OUTCOME-640): live capacity always answers and a non-converging scan stops itself. Rung 2 (OUTCOME-650): quiet guard with capacity ring, reserve alert and change journal; the scanner is retired and the legacy store preserved. Rung 3 (OUTCOME-660): a bounded review of localGit and opted-in caches in under a minute, with measured growth attribution. Rung 4 (OUTCOME-670): agents read the same report, growth and impact through bounded MCP tools. Each rung has its own gate, repeats earlier proofs on the same candidate, and is installable on its own with separate authorization — Each rung has distinct actor-visible value and its own recovery boundary; earlier rungs remove active harm before new capability is added

Decision: Yes, only through measure_path: one path inside configured scopes, 15 s and 500k entries, joining a running review instead of starting a second one. All other tools are read-only over stored reports — The budget, not the absence of work, is what keeps an agent from causing an unbounded scan

Decision: In the bounded review walker: TASK-621 requires TASK-611 directly and its acceptance states the leaf guarantee. TASK-612, which certifies the retired metadata scanner, is superseded with its history and evidence kept — The pruning rule still matters, but only where a walk happens; after rung 2 that is the review walker alone
chronicles.ending: The intent ended with all required primary evidence verified.
